items.title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG
items.summary: EEG-Jev is a single-pass decision model that outputs calibrated probabilities for choices, propositions, and other EEG analysis tasks.
items.whyItMatters: It streamlines EEG interpretation, improving speed and consistency for researchers and clinicians.

items.title: RepoEviAgent: Scalable Synthesis of Evidence-Grounded Repository-Level Question Answering Tasks
items.summary: RepoEviAgent is a framework that builds scalable, evidence‑grounded datasets for repository‑level QA by curating quality data and using specialized agents.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more accurate AI tools for developers by providing richer, structured training data on real software repositories.

items.title: Subliminal Learning Crosses Modalities
items.summary: The paper demonstrates that language models can learn preferences subliminally, transferring knowledge from one model to another via seemingly meaningless data across modalities.
items.whyItMatters: It reveals hidden vulnerabilities in model training, impacting security and bias mitigation in AI systems.

items.title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?
items.summary: The paper introduces CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark to study how mid‑execution environmental changes affect robot policy performance.
items.whyItMatters: It helps designers build more robust robots that can handle unexpected shifts during tasks.

items.title: No Fixed Configuration Is Best: Context- and Cost-Aware Tuning of LLM Pipelines, with an Application to Schema Matching and Mapping
items.summary: Researchers tuned numeric settings of a multi-stage LLM pipeline for schema matching, balancing accuracy and cost, and evaluated its benefits and limits across 35 tasks.
items.whyItMatters: Shows how fine-tuning can reduce costs while modestly improving accuracy in practical AI workflows.

items.title: Start Where the Data Are: Statistical Priors for One-Step Generation on Manifolds
items.summary: The paper proposes a statistical prior for one-step generative models on manifolds to avoid spurious samples in low-density gaps.
items.whyItMatters: Improves reliability of fast generative models for protein design and other scientific tasks.

items.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Malaria Parasite Detection and Species Differentiation in Thick Blood Smear Images: A Pilot Feasibility Study
items.summary: The study evaluates TRACE-Mal, a deep learning system that detects and differentiates malaria parasites in thick blood smears, focusing on explanation reliability.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because reliable explanations improve trust and clinical decision support in AI diagnostics.

items.title: Modeling Event-Conditioned Emotional Expression Response with LLM Agents in a Synthetic Social Simulation
items.summary: The paper proposes using LLM agents to model how emotions influence behavior in synthetic social simulations, aiming to improve predictions in areas like emergency response.
items.whyItMatters: Emotion-aware simulations could enhance planning and response strategies in critical public health scenarios.

items.title: Two-Stage Post-Training for Flow-Based Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage post-training approach for flow-based embodied foundation models, combining supervised fine-tuning and multi-teacher policy distillation to improve task execution.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a practical method to enhance embodied AI performance across diverse tasks, addressing common fine-tuning and reinforcement learning challenges.

items.title: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT
items.summary: The paper tackles how joint-embedding predictive models fail to capture subtle chest CT findings like small nodules due to context shortcuts.
items.whyItMatters: Improving self‑supervised learning could enhance early lung cancer detection in radiology.

items.title: Faithful Persona Steering under Incongruity via Dual-Stream Refinement
items.summary: The paper proposes a dual‑stream refinement approach to personalize large language models, balancing stable persona traits with context‑specific quirks to avoid drift and over‑generalization.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a more nuanced, adaptable way to keep LLMs consistently aligned with complex human identities.

items.title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
items.summary: The article discusses how SWE‑Bench benchmarks use tests from original fixes that may over‑specify requirements, causing valid alternative solutions to fail, and proposes a method to detect such overspecification.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it improves benchmark reliability and fair evaluation of coding agents.

items.title: Gaze World Model
items.summary: Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. items.title: Not All Interpretation Methods Are Created Equal: Tiered Evaluation of AI Interpretability
items.summary: As AI transitions to sociotechnical deployments, uninterpretable models pose serious threats to reliability, public trust and contestability. However, not all interpretation methods are created equal: for interpretability to enhance deployment safety and effectiveness, interpretation methods must be evaluated in a tiered system to differentiate evidence levels of trustworthiness, rather than…

items.title: GaokaoMathGen: Chinese Gaokao Mathematics Finale Problem Generation Controlled by Latent Reasoning Structures
items.summary: Generating Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problems requires controlling not only the included skills, but also the underlying mathematical kernel and solution path. Existing LLM-based methods mainly rely on surface-level specifications, while the realized difficulty of generated problems cannot be determined directly from prompted targets. items.title: Exploring Multi-Player Social Games as Verifiable Training Grounds for Large Language Models
items.summary: The training of socially intelligent language models often relies on large language model (LLM) judges, which are expensive, noisy, and vulnerable to reward hacking. Multi-player social games offer a natural alternative: they require open-ended communication to coordinate with teammates and infer hidden roles, while their rules provide an objective outcome which can serve as a verifiable reward…

items.title: Compressible Representations: Functional Spines in Deep Neural Networks
items.summary: Deep networks embed inputs in high-dimensional representations, but how much of this capacity actually drives behavior? We introduce a framework for identifying, at each layer, the subspace of the representation that is functionally sensitive to the task. Using a matrix analogous to the Fisher information but defined over the hidden representation, we rank directions by their influence on…

items.title: Agentic Discovery of Soundness Bugs in Safe Rust Bindings
items.summary: Rust crates confine unsafe code, such as calls into C or C++ libraries or system calls, behind safe interfaces that must uphold Rust's invariants. If an interface encodes one rule of the code beneath it too weakly, a program written in purely safe Rust can cause undefined behavior. items.title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity in a Proof Kernel and in Lean/Mathlib
items.summary: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. Verification is only part of the challenge.
